title: Theophysics Proof Module Map

canonical_node.axiom: The system is organized by ClaimType, ModuleSlot, and KernelRole, where ClaimType determines what a node is, ModuleSlot determines its job in a proof module, and KernelRole determines what Lean is allowed to do with it.
definitions: ClaimType: the type of claim a node makes (e.g., Primitive, Definition, Theorem, FrameworkCommitment).
ModuleSlot: the role a node plays within a proof module (e.g., Primitive/Base Assumption, Definition, Theorem, Evidence/Prediction/Protocol).
KernelRole: the role Lean is permitted to assign to the node (e.g., candidateAxiom, definitionRole, proofTarget, guardedPremise, metadataRole, auditRole, constraintRole, formalObjectRole).
derivation: The document enumerates 25 modules (M01-M25) and assigns 191 canon nodes to specific ModuleSlots and KernelRoles.
Each module has an output statement, kernel status, risk level, and dependencies on other modules.
The mapping is intended to support a proof kernel in Lean, with some nodes marked as proof targets and others as guarded premises or metadata.
The document itself does not provide formal derivations; it is a structural map.
canonical_node.action: Use this map to assign each canon node to a module slot and kernel role, and to sequence proof development according to module dependencies.
boundary: This document does not provide formal proofs or derivations.
It does not establish the truth of any theological or physical claim.
It does not define the exact formal content of any axiom or theorem.
It does not resolve open problems such as PERSONHOOD or the precise typing of C[chi].
test: Check that every canon node has a unique module assignment and kernel role.
Verify that module dependencies are respected in proof development order.
Ensure that nodes marked as guardedPremise or metadataRole are not used as unguarded axioms in the Lean kernel.
Confirm that proof targets are only those nodes explicitly marked as proofTarget.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a structured mapping of 191 canon nodes into 25 proof modules with explicit kernel roles, enabling a modular approach to formal verification in Lean.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing canon node inventory and their ClaimTypes, ensuring no node is lost or duplicated.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this map is removed, the assignment of nodes to modules and kernel roles becomes undefined, hindering coordinated proof development and Lean integration.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Use as a planning and tracking document; do not treat as a source of formal theorems.

overstatement_risks: Treating module outputs as proven theorems when they are only proposals.
Interpreting the map as evidence for the truth of the underlying claims.
kill_conditions: If any node is assigned a kernel role inconsistent with its ClaimType (e.g., a FrameworkCommitment as candidateAxiom).
If module dependencies are cyclic or missing.
If the map claims proof status for modules marked as 'guarded' or 'outside-kernel'.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the proof-ready modules (e.g., M01, M03, M08) in Lean, while keeping guarded premises as assumptions and metadata outside the kernel.

plain_summary: This document is a structural map of the Theophysics canon, organizing 191 nodes into 25 modules with assigned roles for Lean formalization. It does not provide proofs or establish truth; it is a planning tool. Many modules are marked as guarded or high-risk, and the map itself makes no claims about the validity of the underlying ideas.
